description:
Declare numeric stats on threads (push-ups, steps, km run, money spent), log values, and show them over time. To record an event, use an int stat and log 1 each time it happens: agg sum counts occurrences, agg max shows whether it happened at all.

Subcommands:
  new NAME --thread THREAD --type TYPE --agg AGG — declare a stat in the thread file's frontmatter
  list [--json] — list declared stats
  log NAME VALUE [-d DATE] [-t HH:MM] — queue a value in the buffer
  series NAME [--by PERIOD] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — show the value per day, week or month

Args:
  NAME: lowercase letters, digits and '-', unique across the vault. Put the unit in the name if it is unclear (run-km, spend-zar). For log and series, take it from `stats list`.
  VALUE: a whole number for an int stat; a plain number such as 12.50 for a decimal stat (never 1e3).

Flags:
  new:
    --thread  required. A thread name, 'Kind/Name', or wikilink
    --type  required. int (counts, steps, events) or decimal
    --agg  required. How values in one period combine: sum adds them, last takes the latest, max takes the largest
  list: --json
  log:
    -d / --date  YYYY-MM-DD (default today)
    -t / --time  HH:MM (default now)
  series:
    --by  day, week or month (default day). Weeks start on Monday
    --since, --until  inclusive YYYY-MM-DD
    --json  JSON output; empty periods are null

Examples:
  ["new", "pushups", "--thread", "Topics/Fitness", "--type", "int", "--agg", "sum"]
  ["log", "pushups", "25"]
  ["log", "run-km", "5.2", "-d", "2026-10-24", "-t", "18:05"]
  ["series", "pushups", "--by", "week", "--since", "2026-09-01", "--json"]

Notes:
  Nothing prompts.
  new rewrites the thread file's frontmatter.
  log writes only to buffer.md. `buffer flush` files the value in the thread's daily log. series reads both the logs and the unflushed buffer.
  There is no rename and no delete.
  In text output, an empty period shows '-', not 0.
  Exit 1, nothing written: undeclared or duplicate name, wrong value type, bad -d or -t, invalid or already-declared name for new, unresolvable thread, a bad logged value found by series, or --since after --until.
  Exit 2: usage error, such as a missing argument or an unknown --type, --agg or --by value.
